chunks: Ibn Muskān narrated from Abū Baṣīr who said:

I asked him about a man who performed Tamattuʿ but could not find what to offer as a sacrifice, so he fasted for three days. When he had completed his ritual duties, it occurred to him to stay for another year. He said: 'Let him look to the practice of the people of his land; when he believes they have entered their land, let him fast the seven days.'

key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performed Tamattuʿ (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mutamattiʿ pilgrer who extends their stay in Mecca and cannot afford the sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling for a Mutamattiʿ pilgrim who extends their stay in Mecca beyond the Hajj season, requiring them to perform a new seven-day fast as compensation. The ruling is contingent on 'local custom' (manhal ahli baladih), demonstrating the Shia principle of relying on regional practice to determine the precise timing of the fast—specifically, after the pilgrim's hometown residents have returned home. This highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence where communal practice helps define the boundaries of religious obligations.
